force.title: The Channel Shift
force.signature: The store stopped being where you buy — e-commerce, marketplaces, and direct-to-consumer hollow out physical retail, and only omnichannel or the experiential niche survives.

A \u00b7 The categories that went online: Commodity electronics were the first to move online; specialty stores nearly vanished.
Amazon and marketplaces gutted these categories; survivors go experiential and expert.
Clothing and shoes shift online despite fit friction; stores become showrooms.
B \u00b7 The marketplace machine: The platform takes a cut of everything and sets the terms of survival for sellers.
Brands sell straight to shoppers, cutting the retailer out entirely.
C \u00b7 Who's holding on: Big-box survivors fuse online and store — ship-from-store, buy-online-pickup — or lose.
Expertise, immediacy, and experience are the moats physical retail has left.
D \u00b7 The tensions: Shein/Temu and the end of the de-minimis loophole reshape the price war online.
Thousands of stores close a year; the real-estate and jobs fallout compounds.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: the point of sale moved online; platforms and omnichannel scale win, standalone mid-market stores lose.
